items.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacist asks a currently licensed, nationally certified pharmacy technician to call a prescriber's office about a Schedule VI refill. The pharmacist has approved the call and remains responsible for clinical judgments. The receptionist can confirm the unchanged refill authorization, but the prescriber later calls back suggesting a different dose and frequency. Which actions are within the technician's role? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Perform the final clinical dispensing validation because the prescriber verbally confirmed the revised instructions.
choices.why: Incorrect. Final validation is pharmacist-only; communicating a factual refill authorization does not transfer that duty.

choices.text: Ask the prescriber or authorized agent for an additional refill of the unchanged prescription and record the authorization for pharmacist review.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) allows a certified technician to seek refill authorization and, with pharmacist approval, receive appropriate new or omitted information.

choices.text: Independently negotiate the new dose and frequency with the prescriber and update the therapy instructions without pharmacist assessment.
choices.why: Incorrect. Therapy clarification, therapy modification and conflict resolution are prohibited certified technician activities under 8.04(4)(e).

choices.text: Relay factual information already in the patient's profile that needs no professional interpretation, while notifying the pharmacist of the suggested dose change.
choices.why: Correct. Nonjudgmental factual communication is within the certified technician's approved role, but a therapy decision must remain with a pharmacist.

items.novelty_rationale: Separates factual refill communication from intervening clinical modification; E30-002 tests roles without a changing prescriber message.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician holds an active Board-issued pharmacy technician license. The national certification that previously allowed the technician to work under the 'certified technician' category expired yesterday. A pharmacist wants the worker to continue receiving newly telephoned prescriptions and counting as a certified technician for the expanded supervisory ratio until the examination can be retaken. Which response is required?

choices.text: Use ordinary technician duties, title, and ratio status until the accepted national certification is renewed.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 8.04(3) separately requires reduced scope, ordinary technician title and ratio counting after national certification lapses.

choices.text: Receive new oral prescriptions as a certified technician if the pharmacist initials every order within 24 hours.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pharmacist approval does not eliminate the certification eligibility condition for certified-only functions.

choices.text: Continue both certified functions because a Massachusetts technician license remains current.
choices.why: Incorrect. The state technician license alone does not preserve certification-based delegated scope or ratio classification.

choices.text: Stop all work at the pharmacy because losing national certification automatically revokes the separate Massachusetts technician license.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rules explicitly permit the person to function as an ordinary licensed technician while certification has lapsed.

items.novelty_rationale: Active state licensure survives a national certificate lapse; a three-part scope/title/count consequence not tested as a transition by E30-121.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern with a current intern license completes 9 supervised hours at Pharmacy A on a Monday and 5 supervised hours at Pharmacy B later that same Monday. Both preceptors document the actual work and all other supervision requirements are satisfied. The intern asks to submit all 14 hours for Board internship credit because no individual employer assigned more than 12. What is the maximum credit that may be claimed for that calendar day?

choices.text: Fourteen hours, because the limit applies to a single supervising pharmacist rather than to the intern's day.
choices.why: Incorrect. 247 CMR 8.01(4) imposes a daily credit limit on the intern, not a separate limit per employer.

choices.text: Count no more than twelve hours of approved internship credit for that day, across both pharmacy locations.
choices.why: Correct. The current 247 CMR 8.01(4) permits no more than 12 internship credit hours per day.

choices.text: Nine hours, because only the first approved site worked on each day may count toward the internship total.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation imposes a 12-hour cap, not a rule that only one approved site may count.

choices.text: Five hours, because hours worked at a second site automatically cancel the earlier supervised shift.
choices.why: Incorrect. No provision automatically invalidates the earlier verified hours merely because a second preceptor also supervised.

items.novelty_rationale: Combines two employers in same day without asserting any unverified pharmacist mandatory rest rule.

items.stem: A pharmacist maintains a valid Massachusetts CDTM agreement to co-manage adults' diabetes therapy. During a particular year of the agreement, the pharmacist completes 20 Board-approved CE contact hours needed for ordinary renewal, but none of the activities relate generally to the CDTM diabetes practice area. The pharmacist asks whether the ordinary renewal hours alone satisfy CDTM maintenance. What is correct?

choices.text: Yes; an unrestricted pharmacist license alone waives all CDTM-specific education once the first agreement is signed.
choices.why: Incorrect. 247 CMR 16.02 requires ongoing annual specialty CE throughout the agreement.

choices.text: Yes; any 20 general CE hours necessarily include the separate CDTM education requirement, irrespective of subject matter.
choices.why: Incorrect. The additional contact hours must address practice areas generally related to the particular CDTM agreement.

choices.text: No; every CDTM pharmacist must obtain an extra PharmD degree rather than any ongoing CE.
choices.why: Incorrect. The specific ongoing obligation is at least five additional contact hours, not a second degree.

choices.text: Complete at least five additional approved CE contact hours in the related CDTM practice area each agreement year.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e) describes a continuing five-additional-contact-hour requirement applicable during each year of the agreement.

items.novelty_rationale: Assesses topic relevance and yearly continuation, not E30-086's initial CDTM qualifications.

items.stem: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy intern changes the address and email in the intern's personal life and, separately, changes the legal name after marriage. The intern tells the pharmacy manager and corrects the employer's HR payroll file on the day of the changes. Under the Board's current general reporting rules, which further actions are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Update the intern's own Massachusetts DPH online licensing profile with the new mailing address and email within 14 calendar days.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 20.03(1) imposes a personal online-profile update deadline for each individual licensee.

choices.text: Treat the HR record update as a complete replacement for every individual licensee's Board profile and legal name submission.
choices.why: Incorrect. The employer's records do not fulfill the licensee's direct duty to notify/update the Board.

choices.text: Submit the required sworn name-change statement with valid photo identification and any other Board-requested documents within 14 calendar days.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 20.03(2) requires a formal name-change submission separate from merely telling the employer.

choices.text: Assume no personal reporting is due while the intern license is active, because profile updates apply only to managers of record.
choices.why: Incorrect. 20.03(1)–(2) apply to licensees generally, not only to pharmacies or MORs.

items.novelty_rationale: Separates licensee's own profile/name process from employer HR and on-site credential display.

items.stem: A Massachusetts licensed pharmacy technician also holds a Board-accepted national certification. On November 4, 2026, the technician's certifying body permanently revokes that national certification after its own disciplinary proceeding. Separately, on November 5, the licensed pharmacy receives written notice that its accreditation status has been adversely changed. The technician's Massachusetts state license and the pharmacy's license have not yet been suspended. Which reporting conclusions follow 247 CMR 20.03? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The technician can substitute verbal notice to a pharmacy supervisor for every Board reporting requirement.
choices.why: Incorrect. Employer notice is not a substitute for the applicable report to the Board in the manner it specifies.

choices.text: The technician's loss of certification is a reporting trigger even though the Massachusetts technician license is still active.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 20.03(4) includes loss of certification and does not condition reporting on state license suspension.

choices.text: The pharmacy's adverse change of accreditation must be reported to the Board within 14 calendar days.
choices.why: Correct. 247 CMR 20.03(5) separately makes an adverse pharmacy accreditation change reportable.

choices.text: Neither event needs reporting unless the Board has already begun a disciplinary case in Massachusetts.
choices.why: Incorrect. Certification loss and adverse accreditation each trigger current reporting obligations before any subsequent MA discipline.

items.novelty_rationale: Two differently situated licensees experience independently specified loss-certification and adverse-accreditation events; avoid inventing a generic report for an allegation.
